https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/trm-labs/85d748.description: Build a Safer World. TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure. TRM's government cloud environment gives public sector investigators the same real-time analytical power our commercial customers rely on, and this role keeps that environment fast, reliable, and compliant as it scales. You'll join the Data Platform Serving team, working on the StarRocks-backed serving layer that sits underneath government cloud investigations, alongside the engineer who currently owns this domain solo. This is a chance to build hands-on distributed systems experience in one of the most operationally demanding environments at TRM: a regulated, high-availability government cloud deployment. The impact you will have: You will own performance tuning on the StarRocks serving layer, using AI-assisted query profiling (Claude, internal tooling) to find and fix slow query patterns before they become customer-facing incidents. You will build and harden data pipelines feeding government cloud investigations, using AI code review workflows to ship reliable changes faster in a high-compliance environment where mistakes are costly. You will reduce single-point-of-failure risk on GovCloud data infrastructure by becoming the second engineer who can independently operate and troubleshoot the serving layer, cutting incident response time when the primary owner is unavailable. You will use AI-assisted debugging and log analysis to triage production issues in a regulated environment, turning multi-hour investigations into rapid root-cause fixes. What we’re looking for: U.S. citizenship is required for this role due to government cloud data access requirements. Hands-on experience operating distributed OLAP or serving-layer systems (StarRocks, Trino, ClickHouse, or similar), including query tuning and performance optimization at scale. Experience owning data pipeline reliability and incident response, and comfort using AI tools (Claude, Cursor, or similar) to accelerate debugging, code review, and documentation. Independent ownership mindset: you can pick up an unfamiliar piece of production infrastructure, use AI-assisted research and code exploration to ramp quickly, and take on-call responsibility with minimal oversight. About the Team: The Data Platform Serving team owns the layer that turns TRM's data into fast, reliable answers for the teams and systems built on top of it. We're distributed, not distant: the team communicates constantly across Slack and async docs, with a bias toward direct, evidence-based technical discussion. Decisions are made close to the data: engineers who operate the systems make the calls on architecture and tradeoffs, with input from the broader Data Platform org. We work closely with Forward Deployed Engineering and Product teams to keep the government cloud environment at parity with our commercial platform. Team Operating Rhythms: Weekly team sync to review open incidents, in-flight infrastructure work, and upcoming compliance milestones. Async daily updates in Slack on pipeline health, ongoing tickets, and blockers. Sprint-based planning cycles with clear ownership assigned per workstream. Retro after any production incident to capture learnings and adjust runbooks. Learn about TRM Speed in this position: A production database migration broke search-attribute registration across two environments right before a critical audit deadline. The on-call engineer traced the root cause, shipped a fix, and had both environments passing smoke tests again within the same day. With a compliance deadline days away, the team needed off-cluster backups for the government cloud database with zero prior tooling in place. An engineer designed and shipped the full backup and restore pipeline — three stacked PRs — in under two weeks. Audit log retention needed to jump to meet a new compliance floor with no advance notice. The engineer used AI-assisted config generation to update retention policies across the environment and verify compliance the same week. Life at TRM We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day. TRM moves quickly. We are a high velocity, high ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days. Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving. At TRM, you should expect: Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterate Work that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguity A high level of personal ownership and accountability Close collaboration across teams and functions Frequent, high-touch communication Creative problem solving and out-of-the-box thinking A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment. We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here. At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/resortp.description: About ResortPass ResortPass is redefining what it means to be a hotel guest. We give people daytime access to pools, beaches, spas, cabanas, and other hotel experiences without an overnight stay. We work with more than 2,700 hotel partners across 30 countries. We have served more than 7 million guests and generated hundreds of millions of dollars for our hotel partners. Marriott has signed a global agreement with ResortPass, and Hilton has expanded its partnership with us. We have proven the demand. Now we are building the booking and distribution platform that can bring hotel experiences to many more guests, categories, and channels. Why this role matters Most travel platforms are built around overnight rooms. ResortPass is building the platform for everything else a hotel can offer. A day pass is sold by capacity. A cabana is reserved as a unit. A massage needs a time slot, provider, or room. Events have tickets. Food and beverage may be a product, an add-on, or part of a bundle. Each category has different rules for pricing, inventory, fulfillment, and cancellation. We need one clear booking domain that supports these differences without creating a separate system for every category. That same inventory must be available through ResortPass, hotel systems, distribution partners, and authorized booking agents. We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to lead the technical work and be the primary hands-on builder for the ResortPass API. In your first year, multiple distribution partners and an authorized AI agent should complete real bookings through the same versioned API. You will evolve a production Rails and Postgres booking system used by millions of guests. The hard work is keeping prices and inventory correct, preventing overselling, surviving retries and partial failures, and reconciling systems when they disagree. Your ownership and team You will own the API’s day-to-day technical roadmap and design decisions. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you will write production code, lead focused designs, guide migrations, and operate what you build. You will partner with our Staff Engineer on foundational domain and architecture choices. You will be the primary builder, but you will not work alone. Other backend engineers will contribute and build supply, PMS, and POS connectors using the patterns you establish. Product, Partnerships, and hotel operations will work with you from requirements through production launch. This is one of our highest-impact technical bets. What you build will determine how quickly ResortPass can enter new booking channels and categories. This role works from our NYC headquarters four days per week. The base salary range is $190,000–$210,000, plus equity, based on experience. What you’ll do Build and launch the external ResortPass API. Define stable, versioned contracts for live pricing, availability, holds, booking creation, changes, and cancellations. Make booking operations safe under real failures. Design idempotency, recovery, webhooks, and reconciliation for retries, timeouts, duplicates, and partial success. Evolve the core booking domain. Create clear models and invariants for products, schedules, prices, inventory, holds, carts, and bookings. Make the platform extensible. Prove that a new category such as events or food and beverage can use the shared booking model instead of requiring a separate system. Own the architecture for supply, PMS, and POS integrations. Create reusable connector patterns so other engineers can add partners without reinventing failure handling and reconciliation. Define the data contracts that keep inventory discoverable through OpenSearch. Search is supporting technology for this role, not its primary ownership area. Operate what you build. Set reliability and latency targets, and add the tests, metrics, dashboards, alerts, tracing, and runbooks needed for a critical booking path. Turn partner needs into durable platform capabilities, explain tradeoffs clearly, and raise the engineering bar through practical reviews and mentoring. How we ship We move quickly by building quality from the start. A change is done when it is tested, deployed, observable, and safe to roll back. We use AI tools aggressively, but engineers remain accountable for architecture, correctness, and production outcomes. Explore engineering at ResortPass, including why we work and what we are building next. Tech stack Backend: Ruby on Rails, Node.js Data: Postgres, MongoDB Search: OpenSearch APIs and integrations: REST, OpenAPI, webhooks Infrastructure and observability: AWS, Datadog Testing: RSpec, Playwright Who you are We encourage candidates to apply even if they do not match every line below. You have 6+ years of software engineering experience, or a track record of equivalent impact. You have designed transactional systems, built external APIs or integration platforms, and safely evolved data models in production. You understand relational modeling, concurrency, consistency, asynchronous workflows, and distributed failures. You turn complex business rules into clear boundaries, lifecycle states, contracts, and invariants. You can lead an important system as its primary builder while collaborating on foundational decisions. You care about correctness, testing, observability, and safe rollouts. You communicate directly, listen well, and improve the work of engineers around you. Ruby on Rails experience is useful, but not required. Experience with marketplaces, reservations, inventory-constrained commerce, public APIs, or third-party booking systems is also helpful. We care most about your backend judgment, track record, and ability to learn. What success looks like in 6–12 months Multiple distribution partners and an authorized AI agent complete real bookings through one reusable API. The full booking lifecycle meets agreed targets for correctness, success rate, latency, overselling, recovery, and reconciliation. Reusable contracts and connector patterns materially reduce the work required to onboard the next partner. The shared booking model supports at least one new category without a separate booking system. As the API becomes a company-wide platform, this role can grow toward Staff through demonstrated impact across the booking domain, integrations, and distribution. Benefits Health, dental, and vision coverage, with ResortPass contributing to monthly premiums Stock options 401(k) plan Unlimited paid time off Paid parental leave Annual ResortPass credit for pools, beaches, spas, and other experiences

https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/gamechanger/be4.description: ABOUT GAMECHANGER: We believe in the life changing impact youth sports have on and off the field. Sports encourage leadership, teamwork, responsibility, and confidence – important life lessons that have the power to propel our youth toward meaningful futures. We recognize that without coaches, parents, and volunteers, organized youth sports could not exist. By building the first and best place to experience the youth sports moments important to our community, we are helping families elevate the next generation through youth sports. So if you love sports and their community building potential, or building cool products is your sport, GameChanger is the team for you. We are a remote first, dynamic tech company based in New York City, and we are solving some of the biggest challenges in youth sports today. THE POSITION: GameChanger is launching a Studio team, a small, fast-moving group whose job is to answer one question: is this opportunity worth pursuing? Partnering with our Strategy team, the Studio takes new and emerging business ideas, like expanding into a new sport or entering an international market, and rapidly validates them with real customers. This lets us commit to the right bets faster and stop sitting on promising ideas because we lack evidence. As the founding product manager on this team, you'll pair with a designer to run focused validation sprints. Unlike a traditional product management role, your output isn't a shipped feature or a roadmap of releases. It's confidence: a clear, evidence-backed recommendation on whether an opportunity deserves deeper investment and handoff to a product team, or whether we should walk away and move on to the next idea. You'll operate more like a founder than a feature owner, with no large embedded team behind you, pulling in partners from User Research, Strategy, Data & Analytics, Product, Engineering, and beyond when the work demands it. You will report directly to our SVP of Product. WHAT YOU'LL DO: Opportunity framing: Partner with the Strategy team to translate emerging business ideas into sharp, testable hypotheses. Define the riskiest assumptions, what "validated" looks like, and what evidence would change our minds before any work begins. Validation sprints: Run the Studio's operating cadence with your design partner. Scope each sprint tightly, choose the fastest credible path to an answer, and keep the team moving instead of polishing. Market and business analysis: Size opportunities, model potential business cases, analyze competitive and market dynamics, and pressure-test whether an idea can work commercially, not just whether customers like it. Customer evidence: Get in front of real coaches, players, families, and prospective customers alongside your designer, whether that means surveys, interviews, onsite ethnographic research, demand tests, or prototypes in market. Recommendations: Synthesize customer evidence and business analysis into crisp go/no-go recommendations for leadership, including the honest recommendation to not pursue something. Package validated opportunities for a smooth handoff to a product team to build. Team building: Help define how the Studio operates. As a founding member, you'll shape the playbook, the sprint cadence, the decision framework, and the standard for what "enough confidence" means. Leverage AI: Use AI tools aggressively across research synthesis, analysis, and prototyping support so a two-person team can evaluate far more than its size suggests. WHO YOU ARE: - 5+ years of experience managing technology products, with a focus on mobile or consumer products, ideally including 0-to-1 work such as early-stage startups, new product incubation, or founding a company of your own. - A strategic, business-minded thinker. You're as comfortable sizing a market and building a lightweight business case as you are talking to customers, and you care as much about whether we should pursue something as how we would. - Entrepreneurial, self-motivated, and a doer. You don't wait for a mandate, a researcher, or an analyst. You figure out the fastest path to an answer and go get it yourself. - Comfortable being on a bit of an island. You thrive with high autonomy and ambiguity, and you proactively pull in collaborators rather than waiting for a team to form around you. - Experienced with data-informed decision-making, and capable of running your own analysis to size opportunities and interpret experiment results. - Skilled at customer discovery. You can plan, recruit for, and conduct interviews and lightweight research without a dedicated research team. - A strong communicator who can distill messy, ambiguous findings into a clear narrative, recommendation, and tradeoffs for executives, and who builds relationships and influence across all levels of the organization. - Intellectually honest. You're motivated by finding the truth about an opportunity, not by making every idea look like a winner, and you're comfortable recommending we kill something you worked hard on. - Fluent with (or hungry to master) AI tools for research, analysis, and rapid prototyping, and excited about how they let a small team punch far above its weight. - Knowledgeable about (or passionate about learning) sports and the communities around them. BONUS POINTS: - You've founded or worked at an early-stage startup, or on an incubation, venture, or new bets team. - Experience evaluating international expansion or entirely new market opportunities. - Background in strategy, consulting, or corporate development that sharpened your market analysis and business modeling skills. Perks: - Work remotely throughout the US* or from our well-furnished, modern office in Manhattan, NY. - Unlimited vacation policy. - Paid volunteer opportunities. - Technology stipend - $4,000 every 2 years after your start to make sure you have the latest and greatest technology. - WFH stipend - $500 annually to make your WFH situation comfortable. - Monthly physical, mental, wellness & learning stipend offered through Holisticly. - Monthly lifestyle stipend offered through Fringe. - Full health benefits - medical, dental, vision, prescription, FSA, HRA, HSA, and coverage for family/dependents. - Retirement savings - Traditional and Roth 401K plans are offered through Vanguard, with an immediate company match. - Life insurance - basic life, supplemental life, and dependent life. - Disability leave - short-term disability and long-term disability. - Company paid parental leave - up to 20 weeks for birthing parents and up to 12 weeks for non-birthing parents. - Family building benefits offered through Progyny. - DICK'S Sporting Goods and their family of brands teammate discount.
